sim-engine: a continuous assign that reaches an effectful call runs at time 0 once, after the first batch (§2 🆕 AB)

§4.5.590 — §2 🆕 AB (§5.2 row 1; §4.5.585's fix path). Oracles: iverilog
13.0 -g2012, verilator 5.052 --binary --timing --assert. Verilator is no
oracle on x/z or on time-0 order (2-state; it runs a continuous assign
before or after an `initial` depending on its arguments), so only its
time-0 call count is compared.

Bug: the time-0 settle evaluated every continuous assign before any
process ran, so `assign y = f(a, b);` called `f` on `x` first and again
once the `initial` wrote `a`, `b`: one extra `$display` line (k1: vita
`f t=0 x=x z=x` then `f t=0 x=0 z=1`; both oracles the second only), a
`unique` / `priority` miss in `f` or anything it calls reported W4031 at
t0 (q1caf_case_tbF/L, t0f_ca_case, n_ca_objf2case_tbL x4 through a class
handle, q6a through a formal-less `function void`), an immediate
`assert` failed E4003 and a clean design exited 1 (k2b), a `$fatal`
ended the run at t0 (k2_fatal_x); both oracles silent, exit 0. A delayed
assign evaluated its rhs for its width, and a multi-driver group every
member on every pass, so their calls ran on `x` too (c1_delay 4 calls
on `x`, s4 3).

Mechanism (new `sched/t0_hold.rs`; `levelize/call_deps.rs`
`func_effect_free`; `sched/scan_arm.rs`, `sched/run_loop.rs`,
`native/run.rs`; no IR, format or JIT change):
- Hold set, built once in `Scheduler::new` (`T0Hold::build`): an assign
  whose rhs or lhs index reaches a user call (an exhaustive `sim_ir::Expr`
  walk that holds on any arm it cannot see through) AND (a reached callee
  is not effect-free — `func_read_deps`' walk declines its body, or a
  system task is reachable, transitively — OR the assign reads a heap
  handle, through which a class method's body is out of that walk's
  sight), minus an assign `ca_deps` certifies with an EMPTY read set and
  no multi-driver group (nothing a t0 process writes reaches it, so
  holding it would only reorder a race: a4 `f(1'b0, 1'b1)` keeps PRE's
  place = verilator; iverilog runs it after the `initial`).
- Closure: every assign reading a net a held assign drives is held too
  (worklist over per-net readers), so no assign settles on a held net's
  declared default (x2b: `assign v = (w === 1'bz);` below a held `w`
  settled `v = 1` and the first batch saw a posedge iverilog never fires).
- Hold window: every settle before the first batch is taken (seed,
  initializer re-settle, loop-top) drops a held assign from the pass
  without re-dirtying it; the multi-driver resolution skips a group with
  a held member, `schedule_delayed_cas` and the copy-net repair skip
  held assigns; a held delayed assign drives its initial `x`, sized from
  the lvalue and the rhs's static width without evaluating the rhs.
- Release: the first settle after the first batch is taken (at run start
  when there is none) settles the non-held assigns to a fixpoint, then
  releases the held ones in waves by Kahn counting per net (an assign's
  wave comes once every other held driver of a net in its read set is
  released; when none is ready the rest go in one wave), settling after
  each; the wave that releases an assign marks it dirty. Inside the
  waves each pass visits only the held members of `ca_always`, the
  multi-driver groups with a held member and the held delayed assigns
  (by the closure nothing else reads a held net). A net first dirtied by
  the waves with no definite bit leaves the change list (the arming's T0
  X-DROP, applied again because the hold moved those writes past it).
- Hold-free path: `settle_cont_assigns` tests `T0Hold::active` once per
  call and otherwise runs `settle_cont_assigns_inner::<false>`, the
  fixpoint monomorphised with no hold test in the pass or multi-driver
  loops; `T0Hold` is boxed in `Scheduler`; a design with no call is not
  walked and allocates nothing.
- Native loop top: checks a latched `call_fatal` before and after its
  loop-top settle, as the engine's run loop does, so a `$fatal` a
  continuous assign's call latches ends every backend at its time (k3:
  native ended `(Error) at time 2`, interp / vm and both oracles at 1).

Byte-identity: with an empty seed set `active` is false from
construction, every settle is the pre-hold fixpoint (const-generic copy;
round 3's token diff of PRE's loop vs `inner::<false>`: no divergence),
the release never runs; outside the boundary only the native fatal check
changes behaviour, and only on a latched `call_fatal`. Corpus: stdout +
stderr 22/22 byte-identical PRE vs POST, corpus-runner 10 ok +
verilog-axi ruled-split. The corpus holds 0 assigns (verilog-ethernet's
80 `lfsr_mask` assigns are certified empty-deps, exempt), so corpus
identity is vacuous for the hold path. JIT build = POST on every cell;
`--no-default-features` differs only on the delayed-call product
refusals PRE has; staged vcmp/velab/vrun = one-shot except designs both
binaries refuse at elaboration.

Movers (PRE vs POST vs both oracles, 175 grounding / plan cells x 3
backends, per axis; measured on the round-1 freeze, from which the
shipped tree moves only two lens cells' native output, sd01a/b): 167
cells with an oracle, 106 moved, 0 moved on an axis where PRE = iverilog
= verilator. Call count: 31 -> oracle, 17 neither -> neither. Reports:
39 -> oracle, 12 neither -> neither, 5 iverilog -> verilator (f1, b1p,
v4, v6 x2: iverilog's x call depends on argument spelling, T1, ROADMAP
§0 ⑨). Events: 2 -> oracle (e4, x2d), 1 neither -> neither, 1 verilator
-> neither (e2, a race). Values: 6 -> oracle, 12 neither -> neither, and
on the race axis 6 verilator -> neither, 1 verilator -> iverilog (an
`i0` read of a held output: vita `z` on a net / `x` on a variable,
iverilog `z`, verilator the value or 2-state `0`; ROADMAP §2 Oracle
splits). Lens cells moved to both oracles: d07, d10, d11, d14; to
iverilog: sd02a/b (`final y=z`); closer: d09 calls 7 -> 4 (iverilog 3,
verilator 6), d18 22 -> 18 (both 6), d19 11 -> 8 (iverilog 1, verilator
3), e01 7 -> 5 (both 1).
VCD: the one cell with `$dumpvars` (d15) records the held wires' initial
values as `z`, then `x` / `1` at #0, where PRE and iverilog record `x`
then `1`; the end-of-#0 values agree.

Performance (release, PRE vs POST, discarded warm-up pair then
ABBAABBA, AB and BA ratios agree everywhere):
- nothing held: clk_200k interp 0.90/0.91, vm 0.90/0.91, native
  1.02/1.03 (the interp / vm gain unattributed); corpus native wall per
  row 0.994-1.017 (sha256 ... keccak-arr).
- held chains of certified assigns: chain / wires 1k-16k 1.02-1.07,
  arr / vec / vchain 0.98-1.00, the round-2 lens shapes (fan-in,
  fan-out, rings, call chains) 0.97-1.05, sd_chain_1000_1000 0.27 /
  0.32, sm_chain_1000_250 0.28 / 0.34 (interp / native).
- held uncertified chains are O(N^2) during the release: r_chain (a
  `$random` callee) 250/500/1000 interp 2.70/6.80/16.99, native
  2.78/6.52/16.09; native 1k-8k 15.3/38.9/91.4/198.4x, hu_urandom
  1k-4k 14.4/35.9/81.0x (ROADMAP §5.b T0-HOLD-CHAIN).

Review: 4 rounds, differential + soundness lenses, frozen binaries.
- Round 1: BLOCKING, the release was O(N^3) time / O(N^2) memory on a
  held chain (transitive preds re-scanned per wave: chain_8000 47.7 s /
  189 MB vs PRE 0.05 s / 41 MB); fixed by the per-net Kahn waves and the
  worklist closure (identity probe: old and new wave sets asserted equal
  on 215 cells x 3 backends and the full suite). MINOR: native polled
  `call_fatal` only after its loop-top settle (sd01a/b backend split;
  fixed, the pre-settle check); three unpinned shapes (effectful callee
  through a pure wrapper, two-level closure, lhs-index call; pinned).
- Round 2: MAJOR, each wave settle re-visited every `ca_always` member
  and multi-driver group (sd_chain 2.23x, sm_chain 1.80x) and the
  nothing-held settle was interp +4.5% (clk_200k); fixed by the
  wave-visit restriction and the hold-free monomorphised path. MINOR:
  two mutants (MK1 build threshold, MKA first net only) survived the
  workspace suite, each putting back a call on a held net's default;
  pinned (r2e, r2c). MINOR: a declined callee's body reads are not in
  `ca_deps`' read set (r2h2; PRE also wrong): documented residue.
- Round 3: PASS on both lenses (post_c -> post_d 0 movers on 31 lens
  cells x 3 backends incl. VCD bytes), with the held-uncertified O(N^2)
  as a MAJOR residue (r_chain_500 7.27x).
- Round 4 (D8 scope signal): re-running a held uncertified assign only
  in its own wave made r_chain linear and f07 12 calls (PRE 30, both
  oracles 6), but soundness found a BLOCKING stale value: through a
  declined callee's body read the assign stayed computed on a held net's
  default past t0 (r4a `W2 t=1 w2=0`, r4c, r4d, r4g, and the
  differential's g06 `ev u=0 t=1`: events at t >= 1 in neither oracle).
  Reverted; this commit is the round-3 tree. The fix shape (own wave only
  where the read set is complete) waits on the body-read prerequisite.
Mutants (expected killers written first): 20 (round 1), 26 (rounds
2-3), 28 on this tree, all killed by the narrow run (no survivor needed
the workspace run); round 3 soundness MR, MH killed.

Tests: crates/cli/tests/t0_call_cont_assign_hold.rs (3 backends each,
k1 also staged; oracle text above each pin): k1, k2b,
q1caf_tbF/L, d1-d4, j1, a10-a12, x2b, e4, e7, k7_finish, q8, q7 / q9
(held delayed x-drive, engine and native), n4e (X-DROP), k3, T1, the
waves (b1, s5, r2c, r2e), q5 (a call reading `mem[0]` is held), race
pins (a4, T3, T2b, q3) and residue pins (s4, c1_delay,
n_ca_objf2case_tbL). unique_if_chain.rs: u20's W4020 count 2 -> 1 (u20d
attribution: PRE's two came from the x-run before `dut init`; the one
left is the pre-existing ignored member-handle write on a constructed
object, PROBE_CATALOG), and every 🆕 AB sentence rewritten to POST's
measured output.

Residues (ROADMAP §2 🆕 AB, BLOCKED on a declined callee's body reads in
`ca_deps`): held uncertified chains re-run per wave (f07: PRE 30, POST
42, both oracles 6; the next printed `$random` moves with the draw
count: PRE -887079274, POST -445445430, iverilog -1295874971; x3 4,
d19 8, e01 5 calls where the oracles make 1-3) and per settle pass at
later steps; per-net wave order (d18 18, both oracles 6; e02 9, iverilog
10, verilator 13); a cycle released whole (k01 `f6 t=0 v=z`); body reads
missing from the read set (r2h2 `f2 t=0 x=1 w1=z`, then `w1=0`); k06, a
`$fatal` latched by an assign's call does not stop the rest of that t0
settle (PRE the same). `sched/scan_arm.rs` is now 1929 lines (was
1854), `native/run.rs` 1788 (was 1643).
